Abstract Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is a common precursor state for blood cancers that most frequently occurs due to mutations in the DNA‐methylation modifying enzymes DNMT3A or TET2 . We used DNA‐methylation array and whole‐genome sequencing data from four cohorts together comprising 5522 persons to study the association between CHIP, epigenetic clocks, and health outcomes. CHIP was strongly associated with epigenetic age acceleration, defined as the residual after regressing epigenetic clock age on chronological age, in several clocks, ranging from 1.31 years (GrimAge, p < 8.6 × 10 −7 ) to 3.08 years (EEAA, p < 3.7 × 10 −18 ). Mutations in most CHIP genes except DNA‐damage response genes were associated with increases in several measures of age acceleration. CHIP carriers with mutations in multiple genes had the largest increases in age acceleration and decrease in estimated telomere length. Finally, we found that ~40% of CHIP carriers had acceleration >0 in both Hannum and GrimAge (referred to as AgeAccelHG+). This group was at high risk of all‐cause mortality (hazard ratio 2.90, p < 4.1 × 10 −8 ) and coronary heart disease (CHD) (hazard ratio 3.24, p < 9.3 × 10 −6 ) compared to those who were CHIP−/AgeAccelHG−. In contrast, the other ~60% of CHIP carriers who were AgeAccelHG− were not at increased risk of these outcomes. In summary, CHIP is strongly linked to age acceleration in multiple clocks, and the combination of CHIP and epigenetic aging may be used to identify a population at high risk for adverse outcomes and who may be a target for clinical interventions. Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration are the two important aging phenomenon associated with adverse clinical outcomes. We found that mutations in most CHIP genes were associated with increased age acceleration in multiple epigenetic clocks. extracted_data.document_summary: This large-scale observational study (5522 individuals across four cohorts) investigated the association and synergistic interaction between Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) and epigenetic age acceleration, measured by multiple epigenetic clocks (e.g., Horvath, Hannum, GrimAge, PhenoAge, EEAA, IEAA), with clinical outcomes including all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD). The study found that CHIP is strongly linked to epigenetic age acceleration and reduced methylation-estimated telomere length. Critically, the combination of CHIP and significant epigenetic age acceleration (particularly AgeAccelHG, a composite of Hannum and GrimAge) identifies a high-risk population for all-cause mortality and CHD, with specific gene mutations (e.g., TET2, DNMT3A, JAK2) showing differential impacts on age acceleration and risk. While general inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL6R genotype were also explored, AgeAccelHG proved a superior risk discriminator in CHIP carriers.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Observational study investigating genetic and epigenetic associations.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was a large-scale observational study across four cohorts (FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA) involving 5522 individuals. No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study identified Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) through Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for somatic mutations (e.g., in DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes) from whole blood DNA. Epigenetic age acceleration was quantified using DNA methylation arrays, calculating residuals from various epigenetic clocks including Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, SkinBloodClock, GrimAge, IEAA, and EEAA, and methylation-based telomere length (DNAmTL). A composite measure, AgeAccelHG (Hannum and GrimAge acceleration >0), was used for advanced risk stratification. The study analyzed quantitative associations between CHIP status, specific mutations, epigenetic aging metrics, and clinical outcomes.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Blood (whole blood DNA from hematopoietic cells via DNA-methylation array and whole-genome sequencing)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Presence/Absence of cancer-associated somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells (e.g., DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, ASXL1, DDR genes)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Prevalence >20% in those over 80 years. CHIP carriers were significantly older (+7.23 	 0.61 years, p < 1.13 	 10-31). Associated with epigenetic age acceleration ranging from 1.31 years (GrimAge, p < 8.6 	 10-7) to 3.08 years (EEAA, p < 3.7 	 10-18). Specifically: Horvath (3.01 years, p < 3.0 	 10-25), IEAA (2.92 years, p < 9.3 	 10-26), Hannum (2.71 years, p < 1.8 	 10-23), PhenoAge (2.21 years, p < 1.0 	 10-8), SkinBloodClock (1.58 years, p < 2.5 	 10-13). Associated with reduced predicted age-adjusted DNAmTL (-0.06, p < 1.2 	 10-8); increasing number of mutations (2 mut. vs. 1: -0.174, p < 8.0 	 10-7; >2 mut. vs. 2: -0.404, p < 1.1 	 10-5) led to further decrease. Individually associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.27, p < 0.077). CHIP/AgeAccelHG interaction pooled: coefficient = 0.80, p < 3.7 	 10-3; fixed-effects meta-analysis: coefficient = 0.85, p < 2.4 	 10-3.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A pre-malignant condition characterized by clonal expansion of hematopoietic stem cells that have acquired cancer-associated somatic mutations (e.g., in epigenetic factors), contributing to accelerated aging and increased immune cell dysfunction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Aging and genetic predisposition, assessed in a large multi-cohort observational study (5522 individuals across FHS, JHS, WHI, MESA cohorts) for association with epigenetic age acceleration and clinical outcomes (all-cause mortality, CHD).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A significant predictor of increased risk for developing blood cancers, all-cause mortality, and coronary heart disease (CHD). When combined with epigenetic age acceleration (AgeAccelHG+), it identifies a very high-risk subgroup for all-cause mortality (HR 2.90, p < 4.1 	 10-8) and CHD (HR 3.24, p < 9.3 	 10-6). Also associated with enhanced inflammatory gene expression in mutant macrophages and reduced telomere length.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Calculated residual after regressing epigenetic clock age on chronological age; DNA methylation state at CpGs

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CHIP was strongly associated with epigenetic age acceleration, ranging from 1.31 years (GrimAge, p < 8.6 	 10-7) to 3.08 years (EEAA, p < 3.7 	 10-18). Specific clocks' acceleration with CHIP: Horvath (3.01 years, p < 3.0 	 10-25), IEAA (2.92 years, p < 9.3 	 10-26), Hannum (2.71 years, p < 1.8 	 10-23), EEAA (3.08 years, p < 3.7 	 10-18), PhenoAge (2.21 years, p < 1.0 	 10-8), SkinBloodClock (1.58 years, p < 2.5 	 10-13), GrimAge (1.31 years, p < 8.6 	 10-7). High age acceleration (AgeAccelHG) defined as being greater than 0 for both AgeAccelHannum and AgeAccelGrim.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An indicator of biological aging that is independent of chronological age, reflecting deviations from expected age-related epigenetic changes. It reflects biological aging processes, either intrinsic (independent of cell type) or extrinsic (associated with changes in blood cell type composition and environmental factors), and indicates cellular senescence and increased susceptibility to age-related diseases.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Association with Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) mutations and the overall aging process in multi-cohort epidemiological studies.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with adverse clinical outcomes; when combined with CHIP, it identifies a population at high risk for all-cause mortality and coronary heart disease (CHD), and is a stronger predictor than CHIP alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Epigenetic age acceleration residual, composite measure

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A significant predictor of all-cause mortality and CHD, showing synergistic effects with CHIP for identifying very high-risk individuals. It is superior to hs-CRP and IL6R genotype for risk discrimination in CHIP carriers.
